coding.narrative: On April 25, 2019, a 2019 Tesla Model S with Autopilot engaged ran a stop sign at about 62 mph at a T-intersection on Card Sound Road near Key Largo, Florida, and struck a parked SUV, which hit two people standing nearby; one was killed and one seriously injured. The driver, who had looked down to retrieve a dropped phone, was cited for careless driving and pleaded no contest, with adjudication withheld. In August 2025 a federal jury found Tesla 33% responsible; Tesla's share of the judgment is about $243 million. Tesla filed an appeal brief on November 6, 2026, arguing the distracted driver caused the crash; the appeals court has not ruled.

Electrek reported in November that Tesla's own crash report to NHTSA lists the driver-assistance feature as verified engaged with a pre-crash speed of 71 mph, with the narrative redacted.

coding.narrative: Videos posted on X on November 12, 2026, appear to show a Tesla moving out of the path of a vehicle approaching from behind at high speed in Pleasant Grove, Utah, around November 4 or 5. The person who posted them, who was not in the car, said the Tesla was in self-driving mode. The report says the available information does not establish whether the system or the driver made the manoeuvre, and that police information on a serious collision there does not identify a Tesla as involved. The driver of the speeding vehicle was reported to be in extremely critical condition.
